# 1.35.0: Rosa the fox, and a data archive that takes everything

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are. Model selections
are reset to new defaults once, see below.

## New defaults for every profile

This version resets every profile's model selections and reasoning levels once, including
manually selected models. Later manual changes are kept. Router, SynGuard and Rosa use OpenRouter
models, so they need an OpenRouter key. Keys, conversations and spending records stay.

| Slot | Model | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat | Auto | Selected by tier |
| Light chat | Claude Haiku 5.5 | Medium |
| Heavy chat | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Low |
| Router | Jev 1.14 (OpenRouter) | Off |
| Fast agent | Claude Haiku 5.5 | Off |
| Light agent | Claude Haiku 5.5 | Medium |
| Heavy agent | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | High |
| Chat titles | DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | Off |
| Chat summaries | Claude Haiku 5.5 | Low |
| Rosa | Aion 3.5 Mini (OpenRouter) | Low |
| SynGuard and Normal mode | Jev 1.14 (OpenRouter) | Off |

SynGuard is turned on and web search uses Auto. Old per-slot key assignments are cleared; the
keys themselves are kept. Providers without an available key use the existing model fallback
rules. The reset marker travels with exported settings.

Aion 3.5 Mini always reasons, so Rosa uses its lowest level. More generally, a model that cannot
stop reasoning now gets its lowest level when reasoning is turned off, instead of its own
default level, which is often the most expensive one.

The CMS cryptography dependency is updated to 10.0.13 to address published security
vulnerabilities.

## Decision models for routing and protection

The **Router** slot in **Settings → Models** now also offers OpenRouter models with text input
and decisions output. They choose chat and agent tiers through the Decisions API, with the same
spending limits, cost tracking and fallback tiers as ordinary router models. The selection
survives data export and import. Decisions models are also available for SynGuard.

SynGuard and Normal mode share the selected protection model. A Decisions check asks two
separate questions in one request: is the action safe, and does it need your approval. SynGuard
decides for each call separately. An explicit "unsafe" answer blocks that call; "no approval
needed" skips the question, except for a command scheduled to run later and for MCP tools, which
are always asked about. When a Decisions check fails or gives no answer, a write never
runs on its own: you are asked, and the question says that SynGuard did not check it. Reading
is never held up. New files in Downloads and on the Desktop, and documents the AI created, still need no
approval. Normal mode still reviews approval when SynGuard is switched off, and read-only mode
and disabled tools remain enforced.

Decisions routing uses concise, separate criteria for each tier. Security keywords alone do not
select the heavy chat model: a routine question stays light, while a reported or suspected
threat selects heavy even without evidence or details. Substantial reasoning can also require
heavy. Routing prompts use general criteria without example phrases or scenarios. Safety and
approval prompts judge actual effects instead of alarming words and keep their explicit deny
conditions.

## Meet Rosa

A small pink pixel fox now lives in the window. He comes in a few seconds after the window
opens, so starting the program is not slower, and first sits on the top edge of the message
box, on the right.

- **He sits anywhere.** He stays where you put him: anywhere along the message box, on the
  settings card, on top of the bottom block of the chat list or at the bottom of the window,
  where he settles in a free gap and never covers the buttons.
- **He lives his own life.** He blinks, wags his tail, washes, scratches an ear, looks around,
  lies down and falls asleep when nothing happens. His head follows the cursor, he watches the
  message box while you type and turns to the chat when an answer arrives. Left alone, he finds
  something to do: moves to another spot, struts like on a catwalk, chases his own tail until he
  is dizzy, or invites you to play. One such thing every minute or two at most, and never while
  you type, read a dialog, work in the chat list or use another window.
- **You can see how he feels.** Every feeling has a face, a small icon in a bubble over his head,
  a pose and sometimes an effect. Scared, he crouches and trembles, with waves around his body;
  angry, his tail bristles.
- **He reads along.** Code and science make him put on his smart face. A message about a virus
  on this computer makes him tremble and hide behind the message box, and he is relieved when the
  answer says there is no threat. If you were scammed or feel sad, he comes to comfort you.
  Gibberish or text typed in the wrong keyboard layout puzzles him.
- **He knows the chat is not for him.** Your messages in the chat go to the assistant, and Rosa
  only reacts to them from the side, unless you call him by name.
- **Touch him.** Stroke his head or back with the mouse to pet him, boop his nose, scratch his
  chin, tug his tail (he will not like it). Pick him up by the scruff and swing him, or throw
  him: he flies, bounces off the window edges and lands on whatever is under him. Shaking him
  makes him dizzy.
- **Play with him.** Right click him for the menu: pet, scratch, a treat, a ball to fetch, a
  laser dot to chase, hide and seek, tag, a talk, your friendship, his diary, hide him for an
  hour or until tomorrow. He also starts games himself: he brings the ball and waits for you to
  throw it, peeks out from behind the message box for you to find him, or runs from the cursor
  for you to catch him. Dart the cursor back and forth under his nose and he fights it with his
  paws. Esc or picking him up ends a game; while an answer is being written, Esc stops the answer
  instead.
- **Talk to him.** He answers in a sentence or two with his own model, and can search the web for
  a fact once per conversation. He is a friend, not an assistant: real work belongs in the chat.
- **He remembers.** He keeps your last talks with him and short notes about you that he decides
  are worth remembering. **Our friendship** shows them, and **Forget** erases them. Passwords,
  keys, card and phone numbers are never kept.
- **He has wishes and thoughts.** His model can wish to sulk, make mischief, hide, play, nap,
  cuddle, strut or move, and the program decides whether he may. Now and then he thinks on his
  own, once every 20 minutes at most, without the text of your chats. He gets tired from running
  and rests by napping.
- **He notices what you do.** He peeks out from behind the **Journal** and **PC health**,
  looks around when you open another chat, pricks up his ears when you dictate and sniffs when you
  search or attach a file.
- **Friendship.** Each profile has its own Rosa. Pink eyes mean he likes you, blue eyes mean he
  is cold. Petting, games and kind words warm him up; tail tugs, rough throws and rudeness hurt
  him. Annoy him enough and he lunges at the cursor: two big rows of see-through teeth snap shut
  over it. Forgotten for days, he sulks, then sits in the middle of the message box and demands
  attention. Seriously hurt, he may run off the edge of the window for a while and leave a
  **Call Rosa** paw mark behind. Still offended, he may refuse to come and shout something rude
  from behind the edge, with asterisks; the third call always brings him back.
- **Mischief.** Bored or angry, he may press **New chat** or tap the chat list so it scrolls a
  little. That is
  all he ever does to the program, and never while you type, wait for an answer, select chats or
  have a dialog open. Everything else he does is only a picture: sitting on the send button,
  chewing the model chip, leaving paw prints, turning his back to wiggle his rear at you, sitting
  by the cursor and begging for attention. Mischief can be turned off.
- **His diary.** Every day he writes a short entry about the day before: what you were busy
  with, how much you annoyed and pleased him, whether he bit the cursor or refused to come. With his
  model it is written from the day's numbers, without the text of your messages; without it,
  from a template.

## Rosa's model and your data

- Rosa has his own model slot on **Settings → Models**, Aion 3.5 Mini through OpenRouter at the
  lowest reasoning level by default, and his spending has its own line on the chart, estimated
  on providers that do not report prices. His web searches are listed as web search.
- His model sees only the text you send in the chat, cut to a short length: no attachments, no
  answers from the assistant. Turn off **Read messages with his own model** and he reacts to
  keywords alone and asks no model at all. Without a key he stays quiet and keeps playing.
- His tools are his own: running away, a wish to do something, remembering a note and web search.
  He has no access to the program's tools. His requests are never added to the cost of a chat,
  and when a spending limit is reached he goes quiet instead of asking you.
- His memory and diary live in his own files, encrypted together with your chats when chat
  encryption is on.
- **Settings → Models → Rosa the fox**: show or hide him, three sizes (small, medium by default,
  large), mischief, reading, web search, his own thoughts, your friendship and his memory, his
  diary, call him back, start the friendship over (the diary stays).

## Menu icons

The sorting items of the chat list menu have icons, with the check mark on the right. Rosa's
menu has icons too; they are loaded only when you open it.

## The data archive takes everything

- **Spending for all time** now moves with the settings and is merged by day, so importing the
  same archive twice does not double anything.
- **Recipes and scheduled tasks** were packed before but dropped on import. Now they arrive;
  scheduled tasks arrive turned off.
- **Profile passwords** travel in the archive and are set on profiles that the import creates.
  An existing profile never takes a password from an archive.
- Rosa's memory and diary move with the chats. The archive is still readable by 1.34 after
  going back.
